messages.subject: Dividing neuron data frame
parts:
Hi Dr Jefferis,

I'm currently planning to divide certain neurons into portions whereby each portion of a neuron is arborised in a certain z-coordinate range layer. I was wondering how the package determined EndPoints and BranchPoints. If it is determined by parental connections, would it still be able to find branch and end point when I select only 1 portion of the neuron (e.g. using a dataset with only points contained in the magenta box in the image below)? Furthermore, how would you suggest I approach splitting data of .swc files like this? I hope this email isn't too confusing, thank you for your help!

Best regards,

Ken Nguyen

messages.author: 7e98b49586f8806c
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Dividing neuron data frame
parts:
Hi Ken,

You can divide up the neuron with this function

http://natverse.org/nat/reference/subset.neuron.html 

I believe the end points and branch points are derived from parental connections and will not change after the division. They can be readily accessed using this:

http://natverse.org/nat/reference/rootpoints.html 

best,
arthur

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Dividing neuron data frame
parts:
Thanks, Arthur!

Ken, Arthur is right that subset.neuron should do the trick. Look at the examples in the help page and you should see an example using the coordinates to select points. 

After the subset end points should still be fine.

If you need to be more careful about pruning, because processes double back on themselves, then you can also use the spine function to find the longest path through the neuron, optionally setting the argument to start from the root point. Then you can choose points along that spine closest to a five Z position. Then you can prune_distal from the elmr package to select arbours downstream (or upstream of that location). You might get some additional ideas from the neurons as graphs and neurogeometry vignettes of nat. 

Best, Greg. 

Sent from my iPhone
